european-union.founded_note: Maastricht Treaty entered into force 1 November 1993; institutional roots trace to the 1957 Treaty of Rome (EEC).
european-union.purpose: A political and economic union of European states operating a single internal market with free movement of goods, capital, services, and people, plus common trade, agricultural, and (for eurozone members) monetary policy.
european-union.membership_note: Full members only; candidate countries (e.g. Ukraine, Turkey, Western Balkans states, Moldova, Georgia) and other associated statuses are excluded.

nordic-council.founded_note: Formed in Copenhagen in 1952; Finland joined in 1955.
nordic-council.purpose: A forum for formal inter-parliamentary cooperation among the Nordic countries on legislation, culture, and regional policy.
nordic-council.membership_note: Full members are the five sovereign Nordic states. The Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland participate as associate members (autonomous territories of Denmark and Finland respectively) and are excluded from this list.

nato.founded_note: Signed via the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C., on 4 April 1949.
nato.purpose: A collective-defense military alliance in which member states agree to mutual defense against armed attack.
nato.membership_note: Full members only; partner countries and programs (e.g. Partnership for Peace, Enhanced Opportunities Partners) are excluded.

mercosur.purpose: A South American trade bloc promoting free movement of goods, services, capital, and people among member states.
mercosur.membership_note: Venezuela has been suspended since 1 December 2016 (originally over human-rights and trade-commitment concerns) but remains listed as a full member. Bolivia acceded as a full member in 2024. Associate members (Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname) are excluded from this list.

alba.acronym_expansion: Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America (Alianza Bolivariana para los Pueblos de Nuestra América)
alba.founded_note: Founded by Cuba and Venezuela on 14 December 2004.
alba.purpose: An alliance of mainly Latin American and Caribbean states pursuing political, economic, and social integration through cooperation and mutual aid rather than conventional free-trade agreements.
alba.membership_note: Bolivia was suspended in 2025 after statements by its new government against Cuba, Nicaragua, and Venezuela, but remains listed as a full member. Honduras (2008-2010) and Ecuador (2009-2018) formerly joined and withdrew. Suriname has pending full membership; Haiti and Iran are observers; these are excluded from this list.

comesa.acronym_expansion: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa
comesa.founded_note: Treaty signed 5 November 1993, ratified/entered into force 8 December 1994, succeeding the Preferential Trade Area (PTA) established in 1981.
comesa.purpose: A regional economic community of eastern and southern African states working toward a free trade area, customs union, and deeper economic integration.
comesa.membership_note: Full members only, per the article's current membership list; no members are currently noted as suspended.

asean.purpose: A regional organization promoting economic growth, social progress, and political and security cooperation among Southeast Asian states.
asean.membership_note: Timor-Leste completed accession as the 11th member on 26 October 2025.

eco.founded_note: Founded in 1985 by Iran, Pakistan, and Turkey, succeeding the earlier Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD, 1964).
eco.purpose: A regional intergovernmental organization promoting economic, technical, and cultural cooperation among its member states.
eco.membership_note: All ten states are full members; the founding trio (Iran, Pakistan, Turkey) was joined by the seven others in 1992.

rcep.founded_note: Signed 15 November 2020; entered into force 1 January 2022.
rcep.purpose: A free trade agreement among Asia-Pacific countries that reduces tariffs and sets common rules on trade, investment, e-commerce, and intellectual property.
rcep.hq: Headquartered in No permanent headquarters; the ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta serves as depositary.
rcep.membership_note: Of the 15 original signatories, Myanmar's ratification is excluded here because the ASEAN Secretariat raised concerns about its legitimacy following the 2021 coup, so RCEP is not confirmed in force for Myanmar. India took part in negotiations but opted out before signing and is not a party.

opec.acronym_expansion: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
opec.purpose: An intergovernmental organization that coordinates and unifies the petroleum policies of its member countries to secure fair and stable oil prices.
opec.membership_note: Full OPEC members only; the wider OPEC+ coalition of non-member cooperating producers (e.g. Russia) is excluded. Former members no longer part of OPEC: Qatar (left 2019), Ecuador (left 1992, rejoined 2007, left again 2020), Indonesia (suspended/withdrawn, membership lapsed since 2016-2017), Angola (left 2023), and the United Arab Emirates (left OPEC and OPEC+ in 2026).

pacific-islands-forum.founded_note: Founded 1971 as the South Pacific Forum; renamed the Pacific Islands Forum in 1999.
pacific-islands-forum.purpose: A regional political and economic policy organization for countries and territories of Oceania.
pacific-islands-forum.membership_note: Full members only; associate members and observers are excluded from this list.

eurozone.founded_note: Launched 1 January 1999 with 11 EU member states, following the 1992 Maastricht Treaty's Economic and Monetary Union framework.
eurozone.purpose: A currency union of EU member states that have adopted the euro as their sole legal tender.
eurozone.hq: Headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, Germany (European Central Bank)
eurozone.membership_note: Full EU member states that have adopted the euro only; Bulgaria adopted the euro in 2026. Excluded: microstates Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, and Vatican City, which use the euro under formal agreements with the EU but are not EU/eurozone members; and Kosovo and Montenegro, which use the euro unilaterally without any formal agreement.

visegrad-group.founded_note: Established 15 February 1991 in Visegrád, Hungary, by the presidents/leaders of Czechoslovakia, Hungary, and Poland.
visegrad-group.purpose: A cultural and political alliance of four Central European states that cooperates on military, economic, cultural, and energy matters.
visegrad-group.hq: Headquartered in No permanent secretariat; the International Visegrád Fund is based in Bratislava, Slovakia
visegrad-group.membership_note: Four full members only (Czechoslovakia's founding seat split into Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1993). No formal observer states; Ukraine receives support from the associated International Visegrád Fund but is not a member.

csto.founded_note: Formally established in 2002, evolving from the Collective Security Treaty signed 15 May 1992 among post-Soviet states.
csto.purpose: An intergovernmental military alliance of post-Soviet states providing for mutual collective defense.
csto.membership_note: Armenia has frozen its participation since February 2024 and has announced intent to withdraw, but has not been formally suspended or expelled, so it is retained here. Former members: Azerbaijan (withdrew 1999), Georgia (withdrew after 1993 accession), and Uzbekistan (suspended December 2012, no longer a member).

pacific-alliance.founded_note: Established 6 June 2012, following the Declaración de Lima of 28 April 2011 among the presidents of Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.
pacific-alliance.purpose: A Latin American trade bloc pursuing free movement of goods, services, capital, and people among member states.
pacific-alliance.hq: Headquartered in No permanent secretariat specified
pacific-alliance.membership_note: Four full members only. Singapore is an associated state. Candidate associate members include Australia, Canada, Costa Rica (in process of becoming a full member), Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, New Zealand, Panama, and the United States — none counted as full members.

celac.acronym_expansion: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
celac.founded_note: Formally established 3 December 2011 in Caracas, Venezuela, via the Declaration of Caracas, after being proposed at the February 2010 Rio Group–Caribbean Community Unity Summit.
celac.purpose: A regional bloc of all Latin American and Caribbean states aimed at deepening regional integration outside US and Canadian involvement.
celac.hq: Headquartered in No fixed headquarters; rotating presidency (pro tempore)
celac.membership_note: All 33 sovereign states of Latin America and the Caribbean; excludes the United States, Canada, and non-independent territories.

eccas.acronym_expansion: Economic Community of Central African States
eccas.founded_note: Established 18 October 1983, building on the earlier Customs and Economic Union of Central Africa (UDEAC).
eccas.purpose: A regional economic community promoting economic cooperation and collective self-reliance among Central African states.
eccas.hq: Headquartered in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea (relocated from Libreville, Gabon, in 2023)
eccas.membership_note: Gabon has been suspended since 5 September 2023 following a military coup, but is retained in the list per suspension rules. Rwanda was a member (rejoined 2016) but withdrew again on 7 June 2025 citing instrumentalisation of the bloc by the DRC, and is therefore excluded here.

saarc.acronym_expansion: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
saarc.founded_note: Founded following the first summit in December 1985, after groundwork laid by Bangladeshi President Ziaur Rahman's proposal in the late 1970s.
saarc.purpose: A regional intergovernmental organization promoting economic and regional integration among South Asian states.
saarc.hq: Headquartered in Kathmandu, Nepal (secretariat established 16 January 1987)
saarc.membership_note: Eight full members only. Observers (not counted as members): Australia, China, the European Union, Iran, Japan, Mauritius, Myanmar, South Korea, and the United States.

bimstec.acronym_expansion: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
bimstec.founded_note: Established 6 June 1997 in Bangkok as BIST-EC (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand); renamed BIMST-EC after Myanmar joined in December 1997, and took its current name at the first summit on 31 July 2004 after Nepal and Bhutan joined in February 2004.
bimstec.purpose: A regional organization for multi-sector technical and economic cooperation among South and Southeast Asian states bordering the Bay of Bengal.
bimstec.hq: Headquartered in Dhaka, Bangladesh (permanent secretariat opened 2014)
bimstec.membership_note: Seven full members only; no observer or associate members noted.

cptpp.acronym_expansion: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
cptpp.founded_note: Signed 8 March 2018 in Santiago, Chile, and entered into force 30 December 2018; evolved from the original Trans-Pacific Partnership (signed 2016) after the United States withdrew.
cptpp.purpose: A multilateral free trade agreement reducing tariffs and integrating economies across the Asia-Pacific region.
cptpp.hq: Headquartered in No headquarters; New Zealand serves as depositary
cptpp.membership_note: Twelve full (ratified/in-force) members, including the United Kingdom, which acceded after the original 11 founding signatories. In accession process (not full members): Costa Rica and Uruguay (invited), United Arab Emirates, Philippines, and Indonesia (negotiations pending), and formal applicants China, Taiwan, Ecuador, Ukraine, Cambodia, and Argentina.

oecd.acronym_expansion: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
oecd.founded_note: Established 30 September 1961, succeeding the Organisation for European Economic Co-operation (OEEC, founded April 1948 to administer Marshall Plan aid).
oecd.purpose: An intergovernmental forum of market-economy democracies coordinating economic policy and promoting development.
oecd.hq: Headquartered in Château de la Muette, Paris, France
oecd.membership_note: 38 full members. Countries with accession roadmaps but not yet full members (as of the article's latest update): Argentina, Indonesia, Thailand, Brazil, Bulgaria, Croatia, Peru, and Romania.

melanesian-spearhead-group.founded_note: Began 1986 as a political grouping of Melanesian Pacific states; formally established as an intergovernmental organization on 23 March 2007 via the Agreement Establishing the Melanesian Spearhead Group.
melanesian-spearhead-group.purpose: A sub-regional organization promoting economic growth, trade, and cultural cooperation among Melanesian states and peoples.
melanesian-spearhead-group.membership_note: Full members are Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, and the Kanak and Socialist National Liberation Front (FLNKS), which represents New Caledonia (not yet independent); ISO3 code NCL used for New Caledonia as the FLNKS has no ISO code of its own. Indonesia is an associate member (admitted 2015, not a full member). Observers (not counted): Timor-Leste (since 2011) and the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (since 2015).

schengen-area.founded_note: Schengen Agreement signed near Schengen, Luxembourg in 1985; entered into force in 1995 with the abolition of internal border checks.
schengen-area.purpose: An area of European states that have abolished passport and immigration controls at their mutual borders to allow free movement of people.
schengen-area.hq: Headquartered in None (administered through EU institutions in Brussels, Belgium)
schengen-area.membership_note: Includes 4 non-EU members (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland) participating via association agreements. Cyprus is an EU member obligated to join Schengen but has not yet implemented it; Ireland has a permanent opt-out. Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, and Vatican City are de facto participants (open land borders) without formal membership.

benelux.founded_note: London Customs Convention signed in 1944 by the exiled governments; customs union entered into force in 1948; superseded by the 1958 Benelux Economic Union Treaty (in force 1960).
benelux.purpose: A political, economic, and cultural cooperation framework among Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg.
benelux.membership_note: Full members only; the union has no associate, observer, or candidate categories.

aukus.founded_note: Announced 15 September 2021 as a trilateral security partnership focused on nuclear-powered submarines and advanced defense technology.
aukus.purpose: A trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States focused on defense technology cooperation, including nuclear-powered submarines.
aukus.membership_note: A defense/security partnership rather than a membership organization; no associate, observer, or candidate categories exist.

caricom.founded_note: Treaty of Chaguaramas, signed by Barbados, Jamaica, Guyana, and Trinidad and Tobago; took effect 1 August 1973.
caricom.purpose: A regional bloc of Caribbean states that coordinates economic integration, foreign policy, and functional cooperation among its members.
caricom.membership_note: Eight further territories (Anguilla, Bermuda, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Curaçao, French Guiana, Martinique, Turks and Caicos Islands) are associate members, not full members, and are excluded here. Montserrat is a full member despite being a British Overseas Territory.

african-union.founded_note: Launched in Durban, South Africa on 9 July 2002, replacing the Organisation of African Unity (established 1963); formalized by the Constitutive Act adopted at Lome in 2000.
african-union.purpose: A continental union of African states that promotes political and economic integration, peace, and security across Africa.
african-union.membership_note: Six members are currently SUSPENDED for unconstitutional changes of government: Mali (since 1 June 2021), Sudan (since 27 October 2021), Burkina Faso (since 31 January 2022), Niger (since 22 August 2023), Madagascar (since 2025), and Guinea-Bissau (since 2025); they are retained in this list per AU practice of suspending participation rather than expelling. ISO3 'ESH' is the code for the Western Sahara territory, used here for the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, which has no dedicated ISO code of its own.

igad.founded_note: Founded as IGADD (Intergovernmental Authority on Drought and Development) by Djibouti, Ethiopia, Somalia, Sudan, Uganda, and Kenya; restructured and renamed IGAD in 1996.
igad.purpose: A regional bloc of states in the Horn of Africa that coordinates development, drought response, and security cooperation.
igad.membership_note: South Sudan has been SUSPENDED since December 2021 but remains listed as a member per the article's infobox. Sudan's participation was suspended in 2024 and it rejoined in 2026. Eritrea was a founding-era member that withdrew in 2007, briefly rejoined in 2023, and withdrew again in 2025, so it is not currently counted among the 7 members and is excluded here.

sco.founded_note: Signed in Shanghai, China on 15 June 2001, evolving from the 'Shanghai Five' mechanism established in 1996.
sco.purpose: A Eurasian political, economic, and security organization focused on regional cooperation and counter-terrorism among its member states.
sco.hq: Headquartered in Beijing, China (Secretariat); Tashkent, Uzbekistan (Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure)
sco.membership_note: Observer states: Afghanistan, Mongolia. Dialogue partners (not members): Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Cambodia, Egypt, Kuwait, Laos, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Turkey, United Arab Emirates.

turkic-states.founded_note: Established by the Nakhchivan Agreement, signed 3 October 2009 in Nakhchivan, Azerbaijan (as the Turkic Council); renamed the Organization of Turkic States in 2021.
turkic-states.purpose: An intergovernmental organization of Turkic-speaking states that promotes cooperation in politics, economy, and culture.
turkic-states.membership_note: Observer states: Hungary (since 2018), Turkmenistan (since 2021), and Northern Cyprus (since 2022, not a UN-recognized state).

unsc-permanent.founded_note: UN Charter signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945; the five permanent seats were granted to the principal Allied victors of World War II.
unsc-permanent.purpose: The UN Security Council is the United Nations body with primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security; its five permanent members hold veto power.
unsc-permanent.hq: Headquartered in New York City, United States
unsc-permanent.membership_note: Lists only the five permanent (veto-holding) members (P5); excludes the 10 non-permanent elected members that rotate on two-year terms.

commonwealth.founded_note: Formalized by the 1931 Statute of Westminster; modern form dates to the 1949 London Declaration, which allowed republics to remain members.
commonwealth.purpose: A voluntary association of mostly former British colonies and territories that cooperates on democracy, development, and shared institutions.
commonwealth.hq: Headquartered in Marlborough House, London, United Kingdom
commonwealth.membership_note: Gabon was partially suspended following a September 2023 military coup; the suspension was lifted in July 2025 after elections, so no members are currently suspended.

arctic-council.founded_note: Established by the Ottawa Declaration, signed 19 September 1996.
arctic-council.purpose: An intergovernmental forum of Arctic states that coordinates cooperation on environmental protection and sustainable development in the Arctic.
arctic-council.membership_note: Six indigenous organizations hold non-voting Permanent Participant status: Aleut International Association, Arctic Athabaskan Council, Gwich'in Council International, Inuit Circumpolar Council, Russian Association of Indigenous Peoples of the North, and Saami Council. 13 non-Arctic states hold observer status, including Germany, France, the United Kingdom, China, India, and Japan.

efta.founded_note: Stockholm Convention, signed 4 January 1960 in Stockholm, Sweden
efta.purpose: A regional trade organisation coordinating a free trade area among its members while each retains its own external customs policy.
efta.membership_note: Full members only; no associate or observer categories reported.

baltic-assembly.founded_note: Established 1 December 1990 in Vilnius, following the Baltic independence movements
baltic-assembly.purpose: An interparliamentary organisation promoting cooperation between the parliaments of the three Baltic states on regional and international issues.
baltic-assembly.membership_note: Full members only; no associate or observer categories reported.

five-eyes.founded_note: Formalized by the UKUSA Agreement (5 March 1946), building on wartime signals-intelligence cooperation dating to 1943
five-eyes.purpose: An intelligence alliance for joint cooperation and sharing of signals intelligence among Anglophone nations.
five-eyes.membership_note: No permanent headquarters; cooperation is distributed across each member's national intelligence agencies.

sica.acronym_expansion: Central American Integration System (Sistema de la Integración Centroamericana)
sica.founded_note: Founded 13 December 1991 via the Protocol of Tegucigalpa
sica.purpose: An economic and political organization promoting regional integration, peace, democracy, and development among Central American states.
sica.hq: Headquartered in San Salvador, El Salvador
sica.membership_note: Founding members (1991) were Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama; Belize joined 1998 and the Dominican Republic joined 2013. Excludes any associate or observer states not listed as full members.

ecowas.acronym_expansion: Economic Community of West African States
ecowas.founded_note: Established 28 May 1975 via the Treaty of Lagos, revised 24 July 1993 in Cotonou
ecowas.purpose: A regional economic union promoting economic integration and collective self-sufficiency across West Africa.
ecowas.membership_note: Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger formally withdrew 29 January 2025 (after 2024 exit announcements) and are excluded from this list. Guinea-Bissau remains a member but has been suspended since 29 November 2025 following a coup d'état; suspension is a status change, not loss of membership, so it is retained in the members array. Guinea's earlier suspension was lifted 28 January 2026.

arab-maghreb-union.founded_note: Treaty signed 17 February 1989 in Marrakech, Morocco
arab-maghreb-union.purpose: A political and economic union aiming at cooperation and eventual integration among the Arab states of North Africa.
arab-maghreb-union.membership_note: Full members only; the union's institutions have been largely dormant for extended periods but the five founding states remain the members.

gcc.founded_note: Charter signed 25 May 1981 in Abu Dhabi, UAE
gcc.purpose: A regional political, economic, and military union among Arab states bordering the Persian Gulf.
gcc.membership_note: Full members only; excludes non-member dialogue partners.

cis.founded_note: Belovezha Accords signed 8 December 1991 in Belarus; Alma-Ata Protocol 21 December 1991 following the dissolution of the Soviet Union
cis.purpose: A regional intergovernmental organization coordinating economic, political, and military cooperation among most former Soviet republics.
cis.hq: Headquartered in Minsk, Belarus (with institutions also based in Moscow, Russia)
cis.membership_note: Turkmenistan is only an associate/participating member (since 2005) and never ratified the CIS Charter, so it is excluded from the members array. Ukraine took part in founding agreements but never ratified the Charter and ceased participation in 2018; it is not counted as a member. Georgia withdrew effective 18 August 2009 following the Russo-Georgian War. Moldova has announced withdrawal, effective 8 April 2027, but remains a full member as of this writing and is included here.

g7.founded_note: Originated 1973 as an informal finance-minister grouping (the 'Library Group') formed amid the 1973 oil crisis; formalized as the G7 with leaders' summits from 1975
g7.purpose: An informal forum of major advanced economies for coordinating policy on global economic, security, and climate issues.
g7.membership_note: Not based on a treaty and has no permanent secretariat; the presidency rotates annually among members. The European Union participates in all meetings as a 'non-enumerated member' alongside the seven states but is not counted as one of the seven and is excluded from the members array.

cplp.acronym_expansion: Community of Portuguese Language Countries (Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa)
cplp.founded_note: Founded 17 July 1996 at the 1st CPLP Summit in Lisbon, Portugal
cplp.purpose: A multilateral forum deepening cultural, economic, and political cooperation among Portuguese-speaking (Lusophone) countries.
cplp.membership_note: Full members only; excludes associate observer states.

eea.founded_note: EEA Agreement signed 2 May 1992 in Porto; entered into force 1 January 1994
eea.purpose: Extends the EU single market (free movement of goods, services, capital, and people) to non-EU EFTA states.
eea.hq: Headquartered in No single headquarters; joint EU/EFTA institutions split between Brussels and Geneva
eea.membership_note: All 27 EU member states plus 3 of the 4 EFTA states (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway); Switzerland is an EFTA member but is not part of the EEA, participating instead through bilateral treaties.

cefta.founded_note: Signed 21 December 1992 in Kraków, Poland; entered into force 1994
cefta.purpose: Promotes free trade in goods and services among Western Balkan and other non-EU European states.
cefta.membership_note: Original 1992 members (Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia) and later joiners (Slovenia, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia) all withdrew upon EU accession; today's members are Western Balkan states plus Moldova. Kosovo has no assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code.

quad.founded_note: Initiated by Japanese PM Shinzo Abe in 2007, lapsed, then revived as an annual leaders' summit starting 2017/2021
quad.purpose: An informal strategic security and diplomatic forum among four Indo-Pacific democracies to counterbalance China's regional influence.
quad.hq: Headquartered in None; informal dialogue with no permanent secretariat
quad.membership_note: Not a treaty organization; no observers, associates, or formal accession process. 'Quad Plus' ad hoc outreach partners (e.g. South Korea, Vietnam, New Zealand) are not members.

andean-community.founded_note: Cartagena Agreement signed 26 May 1969 as the Andean Pact; reorganized as the Andean Community in 1996
andean-community.purpose: Pursues economic and social integration among Andean South American states through a free trade area and partial customs union.
andean-community.membership_note: Chile is an associate member (left as full member in 1976, rejoined as associate in 2006), not counted here. Venezuela withdrew as a full member in 2006.

sadc.founded_note: Windhoek Declaration and Treaty adopted 17 August 1992, transforming the earlier SADCC (founded 1980)
sadc.purpose: Promotes regional socio-economic development, political cooperation, and security integration among Southern and Central African states.
sadc.membership_note: Full members only; Comoros joined in 2017. No associate/observer tier distinguished on the article's member list.

cemac.acronym_expansion: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
cemac.founded_note: Treaty of N'Djamena signed 1994; formally replaced the earlier UDEAC in June 1999
cemac.purpose: Promotes sub-regional economic integration and monetary union among Central African states sharing the Central African CFA franc.
cemac.hq: Headquartered in Institutions split across cities: Commission in Bangui, Bank of Central African States (BEAC) in Yaoundé, Court of Justice in N'Djamena, Parliament in Malabo
cemac.membership_note: All six members share the Central African CFA franc as common currency.

arab-league.founded_note: Alexandria Protocol (1944); founded in Cairo on 22 March 1945
arab-league.purpose: Coordinates political, economic, and cultural cooperation among Arab states and safeguards their independence and sovereignty.
arab-league.membership_note: Syria was suspended from 2011 to 2023 over its civil war crackdown and was reinstated on 7 May 2023; it is retained here as a full member. Egypt and Libya were also suspended in the past (1979-1989 and 2011 respectively) and are currently active.

eaeu.founded_note: Treaty signed 29 May 2014 in Astana, Kazakhstan; entered into force 1 January 2015
eaeu.purpose: A post-Soviet economic union providing for free movement of goods, services, capital, and labor and coordinated macroeconomic policy.
eaeu.hq: Headquartered in Moscow, Russia (Eurasian Economic Commission); Minsk, Belarus (Court of the EAEU)
eaeu.membership_note: Observer states (Cuba, Moldova, Uzbekistan) are not full members and are excluded here.

g20.founded_note: Formally established 26 September 1999 in response to the late-1990s emerging-market debt crises; upgraded to a leaders' summit in 2008
g20.purpose: Brings together the world's major economies to coordinate policy on global economic stability, trade, and financial regulation.
g20.hq: Headquartered in None; no permanent secretariat, rotating annual presidency hosts a temporary secretariat
g20.membership_note: The European Union has been a member since the G20's inception (1999), and the African Union joined as the 21st member in 2023; both are institutional (bloc) members and are excluded from this country-only list.

d8.founded_note: Founded in Istanbul, Turkey; first summit held in 1997
d8.purpose: Promotes economic cooperation and development among major Muslim-majority developing economies across finance, trade, and industry.
d8.membership_note: Azerbaijan was admitted as the ninth member on 19 December 2024, expanding the group beyond its original eight founding states.

council-of-europe.founded_note: Established by the Treaty of London, signed 5 May 1949
council-of-europe.purpose: An international organisation that works to uphold human rights, democracy, and the rule of law across Europe.
council-of-europe.membership_note: Russia was expelled in 2022 following its invasion of Ukraine, and is not a member. Kosovo is not a member. Committee of Ministers observer states are Canada, the Holy See, Japan, Mexico, and the United States; Parliamentary Assembly observers are Canada, Israel, and Mexico.

bsec.acronym_expansion: Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation
bsec.founded_note: Founded via the Summit Declaration and Bosphorus Statement signed in Istanbul, 25 June 1992
bsec.purpose: A regional organization promoting multilateral economic and political cooperation, peace, and stability among Black Sea countries.
bsec.membership_note: Observer states include Austria, Belarus, Croatia, Czech Republic, Egypt, France, Germany, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Poland, Slovakia, Tunisia, and the United States.

oas.founded_note: Charter signed in Bogotá, Colombia, 30 April 1948
oas.purpose: A hemispheric organization promoting cooperation among American states on democracy, human rights, security, and development.
oas.hq: Headquartered in Washington, D.C., United States
oas.membership_note: Cuba's government was excluded from active participation in 1962; the suspension was formally lifted in 2009, but the Cuban government declared it would not return, so Cuba is not counted among the 33 active members. Venezuela notified the OAS of its withdrawal in 2017 (effective 2019) under the Maduro government, but the opposition-recognized representative sought to remain in the organization, so Venezuela's status is disputed and it is still listed as a member in the OAS infobox.

usmca.founded_note: Signed 30 November 2018 (revised text signed 10 December 2019); entered into force 1 July 2020, replacing NAFTA (in force since 1994)
usmca.purpose: A trilateral free trade agreement governing trade and investment among the United States, Mexico, and Canada.
usmca.membership_note: A trade agreement among three parties rather than an organization with a secretariat or additional membership tiers.

eac.founded_note: Originally founded 1967, dissolved 1977; re-established by treaty and entered into force 7 July 2000
eac.purpose: A regional intergovernmental organization promoting economic, political, and social integration among East African states.
eac.membership_note: Membership expanded beyond the original five (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi) with South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Somalia.

waemu.acronym_expansion: West African Economic and Monetary Union
waemu.founded_note: Established by treaty signed in Dakar, 10 January 1994
waemu.purpose: A regional organization promoting monetary union and economic integration among West African states that share the CFA franc.
waemu.hq: Headquartered in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso (Commission headquarters; other institutions are seated in Dakar, Abidjan, and Lomé)
waemu.membership_note: Full members only; all eight also share the West African CFA franc.

oic.founded_note: Founded following a summit in Rabat, Morocco, 25 September 1969
oic.purpose: An intergovernmental organization representing the collective interests of Muslim-majority states.
oic.membership_note: Syria's membership was suspended in August 2012 and restored to full membership on 7 March 2025; it is counted among the 57 current members.

apec.founded_note: Founded following a ministerial meeting in Canberra, Australia, 1989
apec.purpose: An inter-governmental forum promoting free trade and economic cooperation among Pacific Rim economies.
apec.membership_note: APEC calls its participants 'member economies' rather than states, reflecting its one-China-sensitive framing. Hong Kong participates as 'Hong Kong, China' (HKG) and Taiwan participates as 'Chinese Taipei' (TWN) rather than under a sovereign-state name.

brics.founded_note: BRIC grouping formed 16 June 2009; South Africa joined 24 December 2010, forming BRICS. Expanded 1 January 2024 to add Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates; Indonesia joined 6 January 2025.
brics.purpose: An intergovernmental grouping of major emerging economies that coordinates economic and diplomatic policy as a counterweight to Western-dominated institutions.
brics.membership_note: No formal headquarters; the associated New Development Bank is based in Shanghai, China. A separate 'partner country' tier below full membership includes Algeria, Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Turkey, Uganda, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam as of October 2024. Saudi Arabia was invited to join in 2024 but, per the Wikipedia infobox, has not been confirmed as a full member despite appearing as joined on BRICS's own website.

mikta.founded_note: Formed 25 September 2013 on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York
mikta.purpose: An informal, cross-regional consultative partnership among five middle-power G20 members to deepen ties and find common ground for cooperation.
mikta.membership_note: An informal grouping with no treaty, secretariat, or formal accession process beyond the five founding states.
